title: fix(lint)!: a flow condition's text-vs-number comparison gets a true verdict on every flow, record.x read and decision branch
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBNYbz7uNdbM42gPou4qdDn8)_

Fixes #29959

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：流程条件里「文本或布尔字段和数字比大小」(如 `name > 5`)现在每个位置都拿到真实判词。记录触发流程里写成 `record.name > 5`、或写在 `decision` 分支里，发布时和裸字段名一样被拒(error，文案说运行在该条件处失败、触发写入照常落库)；非记录触发流程(定时、API、手动/动作启动)仍是 warning，但文案从「静默得到 null」改为如实说明：条件出错时运行失败。MCP `validate_expression` 新增可选输入 `severity`(校验规则)和 `triggerKind`(流程触发方式)，答案与发布门一致。
- **为什么改**：#29926 之后还有三处判词缺失或失真：非记录触发流程的 warning 说「得到 null」(实际 `evaluateCondition` 在每种流程上都抛错、运行失败)；`record.x` 从不做类型判断；`decision` 分支没有字段类型，`name > 5` 运行必失败却无任何提示。MCP 工具也无法表达规则严重级别和流程触发方式，答案与发布门不一致。
- **风险与回滚**：收窄发布门：已有记录触发流程若在 `record.x` 读取或 decision 分支里有这种比较，下次发布会被拒(它们每次运行本来就会失败)。流程条件上的 warning 代码由 `type-mismatch` 改为 `type-mismatch-run-may-fail`(18.3.0 的 formula / mcp 在流程条件上发的是 `type-mismatch`，按代码识别的使用方需改认)。MCP 新输入均可选，不传时答案与之前相同。回滚即 revert 本 PR，无数据迁移。
- **先看**：`packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`(`firstTypeMismatch` 的 record 根第二遍)、`packages/formula/src/validate.ts`(`type-mismatch-run-may-fail` 分支)、`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`(`checkDeclaredPredicate` 的 decision 分支走 `check()`)。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/publish-type-mismatch-fail-closed.test.ts`，预期 9 条全过：记录触发流程 `record.name > 5` 与 decision 分支 `name > 5` 被拒且文案说运行失败；定时流程同样写法发布成功、warning 文案说运行失败而不说 null；类型正确的对照发布无判词。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地(收窄，席位在落地前做 contract review)。

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the author-time gate (`os build`, `os validate`, the package publish and the flow publish door) refuses, on a record-triggered flow, a `type-mismatch` in a `decision` branch and in a `record.FIELD` / `previous.FIELD` read of a start or edge condition, which it passed with no verdict before; refuses the same on a time-relative flow sweeping the object its conditions are typed against, where 18.3.0 served a warning; and a flow condition's `type-mismatch` warning is served under its own code `type-mismatch-run-may-fail` instead of `type-mismatch`. Added beside them (the widening half): the optional `severity` and `triggerKind` inputs of the `validate_expression` MCP tool, the code `type-mismatch-run-may-fail` in `@objectstack/formula`'s `ExpressionRefusalCode`, the optional `flowVariables` key of `@objectstack/formula`'s `ExprSchemaHint`, and a bare flow-condition name that a declared flow variable or node id holds is no longer typed as the field it shadows (no verdict where 18.3.0 served a `type-mismatch` warning).
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: updated here — `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` (the type-soundness row names the decision branch, the `record.FIELD` read and the warning on other flows) and the MCP skill text in `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` (the two new `validate_expression` inputs); `skills/**` teaches no text-vs-number comparison in a flow condition (grep for `type mismatch`, `evaluates to null`, `validate_expression` and the decision examples), so no skill or eval moves.

## What changes

Re-measured on `main` at `73a3ef9f` (after #29953 `9037b13d`). The four sites, and what each now gets:

| site | runtime on a fault (measured) | before | now |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| record-triggered flow: `record.FIELD` / `previous.FIELD` in a start or edge condition | `seedRunVariables` binds the trigger record as `record` AND flattened to bare names, so `record.name` is the bare `name`; `evaluateCondition` throws, the run fails, the write lands | no verdict (the flattened typing left `record` a `dyn` map) | **error** `type-mismatch-run-fails`, the bare name's verdict |
| record-triggered flow: `decision` branch `config.conditions[].expression` | `builtin/logic-nodes.ts` evaluates it over the same run variables, through the same `evaluateCondition` | no verdict (`checkDeclaredPredicate` passed no schema hint); the null-guard twin alone refused | **error** `type-mismatch-run-fails` |
| any other flow (no `triggerType`, `schedule`, time-relative, `api`), all three slots; an inert node `condition` | `evaluateCondition` throws on every flow, so "silently evaluates to null" was false; but the run holds what its entrance hands it | warning `type-mismatch`, "silently evaluates to null" (start/edge only) | **warning** `type-mismatch-run-may-fail`, worded for the failed run (start, edge, decision, `record.FIELD`) |
| MCP `validate_expression` | — | `validation` always fail-closed, `flow_condition` always run-fails | optional `severity` / `triggerKind` inputs; each combination answers the gate's verdict |

**Site 1, grading (seat's ruling: grade as #29953 did if the same runtime fact holds; keep the warning with true text if a reason is measured).** I kept the warning, and the reason is measured on the entrances, not assumed. The run does fail on a fault in every flow (`dag-traversal.ts` `evaluateCondition`, ADR-0032 §1c). What differs is whether the condition faults at all: on a record-triggered flow the bare name and `record.FIELD` are the materialized trigger record (`record-change-trigger.ts` `buildContext` → `seedRunVariables`), so a text field holds text and `name > 5` faults unless the text is numeric. On any other flow `seedRunVariables` binds whatever `context.record` the entrance hands over (`engine.ts` celScope docblock, #22642): the inbound hook's request body (`trigger-api`, a JSON body whose `name` may be a number), a `type: 'flow'` action's loaded row or an empty record carrying only `id`, a parent flow's record (`subflow` / `map`), or nothing for a cron schedule or the REST trigger route. So the object's field type is not proven to be what the name holds, and refusing there would refuse conditions that can run. This is the same measurement that keeps the nullable-comparison twin off those flows (`validate-null-guards.ts` ledger, "sparse or unknown"). The warning now says what happens when it does fault: "a flow condition that faults when it is evaluated fails the run: the flow stops at this condition and the work it exists to do is not done (it does not read null)", and why it is a warning.

**Where the text is decided (`@objectstack/formula`).** A `'flattened'` scope is a flow condition, the only caller that passes one with field types (lint's flow walk, the engine's registration advisory pass, MCP `flow_condition`). So `typeSoundnessIssue` serves `type-mismatch-run-may-fail` for a flattened site with no declared outcome, and the `record`-scoped `type-mismatch` (formula fields, display predicates: there a fault reads null or never refuses) keeps its code and text. The engine's registration log line reads the new text too (it passes no outcome).

**Site 2, `record.FIELD` (`cel-engine.ts` `firstTypeMismatch`).** The flattened typing binds fields bare and leaves `record` / `previous` `dyn`. When that first pass finds nothing and the source reads `record.` or `previous.`, a second pass types those two roots with the `record`-scope struct (`buildTypedEnv(…, flattenedRecordRoots)`), for the text/boolean mismatch only, and `offendingRecordRead` names the read as written (`record.title`). Same judge, same schema hint, same outcome; no second judge. The date verdicts stay the bare name's alone (see Acceptance notes).

**Site 3, `decision` branches (`@objectstack/lint`).** `checkDeclaredPredicate` takes an optional `flowCondition` hint; a `decision` node passes `{ objectName, faultOutcome: flowFaultOutcome }` and the slot goes through the same `check()` an edge goes through. So the branch gets the object's fields and types and the flow's ledger outcome (`run-fails` on a record-triggered flow, none elsewhere). The other declared `predicate` slots (a screen field's `visibleWhen`) bind the screen's collected values and keep the hint-less call. The `faultOutcomeOf` ledger docblock now carries the decision row, the `record.FIELD` reading and the "any other flow" row with its reason.

**Site 4, MCP (`mcp-http-tools.ts`).** I took the "add the inputs" option. `severity` (`error` | `warning` | `info`, default `error`) and `triggerKind` (`FLOW_TRIGGER_KINDS` from `@objectstack/spec/automation` plus `none`, default `record_change`). `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP[site].faultOutcome` is now a function of the two, mirroring lint's `faultOutcomeOf` (validation: `warning`/`info` → `fail-open`, else `fail-closed`; flow_condition: `record_change` → `run-fails`, else none). A call that passes neither answers exactly as before. An input on a site it does not describe is refused as a tool error ("`severity` describes a validation rule; it applies only with site \"validation\" …"). The tool description and the served skill text name both inputs. This is a widening of a published tool schema, declared in the `Clause-②` line.

**`@objectstack/spec`.** New semantic entry `18.flow-record-read-and-decision-type-mismatch-refused`, the changeset's ADR-0087 disposition (`registered`). The #29953 entry `flow-condition-type-mismatch-refused` is left as is: its text (start and edge, bare name; other flows keep a warning) is still true.

## Tests

- `packages/formula/src/expression-refusal-codes.test.ts`: `PINS` for `type-mismatch-run-may-fail` (bare text, `record.active` boolean: exact params and message). `SWEEP_SCHEMAS` gains a flattened deal schema with no outcome, so the sweep reaches the new code and holds its params to its message.
- `packages/formula/src/validate.test.ts`: `record.name`, `previous.name`, `record.is_active` in a flattened `run-fails` site → `type-mismatch-run-fails` naming the read; controls `size(record.name) > 5`, `double(record.name) > 5`, `record.amount > 5`, `record.name == 'x'`, `record.is_active == true` clean. Flattened with no outcome → `type-mismatch-run-may-fail`, not "evaluates to null"; the record-scope warning keeps `type-mismatch`.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts`:
  - #29953's pin "keeps the warning on a flow that is not record-triggered" is updated as the order asks: three flows (no `triggerType`, `schedule`, `type: 'api'`), start + decision + `record.title` edge all `warning`, every message "fails the run", none "evaluates to null" or "still lands";
  - new: record-triggered flow, `record.title` start, two decision branches (bare text, `record.won` boolean), `previous.title` edge → four `error`s with their key paths and the run-fails text;
  - new control: the well-typed versions on the same sites → no type verdict and no error;
  - the #5017 receiver meta-test tables the `flowCondition` plumbing receiver.
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-validate-expression.test.ts`: gate parity. For each `severity` (omitted, `error`, `warning`, `info`) and each `triggerKind` (omitted, `record_change`, `time_relative`, `schedule`, `api`, `none`), the tool's `(severity, message)` list equals `validateStackExpressions`'s on the same rule or flow. An input on the wrong site is refused; well-typed conditions are clean at every input.
- `packages/objectql/src/publish-type-mismatch-fail-closed.test.ts`, new top-level `describe` in the existing harness: through the real `saveMetaItem` (draft) + `publishPackageDrafts` door, a record-triggered `record.name > 5` start condition and a `name > 5` decision branch are refused with the run-fails text; the same comparisons on a `schedule` flow publish with two warnings saying the run fails; a well-typed control publishes clean.

## Acceptance notes

- **Date verdicts in a flow condition still say "silently evaluates to null".** `date-arithmetic` / `date-text-arithmetic` on a bare date field in a flow condition are errors whose text says the field reads null; in a flow the run fails instead. Pre-existing, and outside this card's type-mismatch scope, so the `record.FIELD` pass here deliberately does not extend the date verdicts to `record.d + 1` (it would serve that false sentence at a new site). Reported to the seat as a finding.
- **A declared flow variable named like a text field.** A record-triggered flow that declares `variables: [{ name: 'title', type: 'number', defaultValue: 3 }]` over a text field `title` gets `title > 5` refused as `type-mismatch-run-fails` ("`title` holds text"), though the run seeds the declared variable first and the flattening skips a bound name, so the condition reads the number (measured through the built lint dist on this head; the shadowing warning fires beside it). Present on `main` since #29953, the same on this branch; the type judge reads the object's field types without the declared-variable exclusion the null-guard twin applies (`nullGuardBare`). Fixing it needs the hint to exclude names from the bare typing but not from `record.FIELD`, a new schema-hint key; reported to the seat as a finding, not fixed here.
- **Advisory and inert sites unchanged in grading.** An inert node `condition` keeps a warning (now the run-may-fail text, which is true: it fails the run if it is ever evaluated, and `flow-inert-node-condition` says it is not).
- **Serial check.** None of the 16 open PRs at 2026-11-04T05:20Z touches `packages/formula/src/{validate,cel-engine,expression-refusal}.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` or `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` (the nearest: #29998 metadata-protocol split, #29993 spec conversions registry split; #29963 is version packages).

## Rework after the contract review (head 6a3a1e2c)

- **A bare name a flow variable holds is not typed as the field.** `seedRunVariables` seeds the flow's declared variables and node outputs before it flattens the record, and the flattening skips a bound name. New optional `ExprSchemaHint.flowVariables` (a widening): lint passes the flow's `collectFlowVariableNames` set plus the engine-bound names at the start, edge, decision and inert node sites, and the type judge leaves those bare names `dyn` (date verdicts too), while `record.NAME` / `previous.NAME` stay typed. This also closes the start/edge instance on main from #29953.
- **Time-relative sweeps are graded `run-fails`.** `time-relative-trigger.ts` launches each run with `{ record: row }`, a stored row of the swept object, so on a flow whose `timeRelative.object` is the start node's `objectName` (or is omitted) the ledger, `faultOutcomeOf` and the MCP `flow_condition` map answer `run-fails`. A sweep of another object keeps the warning. The null-guard twin stays on record-triggered flows.
- **Wording.** The run-may-fail sentence no longer asserts the flow's kind (it is also served on inert node conditions and in the registration log); the stale `check()` and `ExprSchemaHint.fieldTypes` comments are refreshed.
- **New pins.** lint: time-relative default / same object (errors) vs another object (warnings) at start, decision and edge; a record-triggered flow declaring `title` as a number variable: bare `title > 5` at start, edge and decision gets no type verdict (shadow warning only), `record.title > 5` stays refused; the #5017 table gains the `sweep` receiver against `TimeRelativeTriggerSchema`. formula: `flowVariables` leaves bare names untyped and keeps `record.` / `previous.` typed. mcp: each trigger kind's severity pinned, not only parity.
- **Ablations.** B1 lint hint not passed: 1 failed. B2 lint time-relative grading off: 1 failed. B3 formula `bareShadowed` ignored: 1 failed. B4 mcp time-relative off: 1 failed. Each restored, blob == HEAD.
